props.title: René Moffatt
props.face: His own songs and covers, solo to four piece.
props.lede: A song nobody at the table has heard before, sung over an acoustic guitar, and by the second chorus the conversation has stopped to listen. René Moffatt writes his own folk and Americana songs, the kind that sit on a playlist beside Josh Ritter and The Avett Brothers. He plays solo for welcome drinks, a patio or a dinner where people listen, brings his band, René Moffatt & The Moonshadows, when the night wants one, and plays covers beside his own songs when you ask.

props._notes: The client strip, the same block the other act pages carry.

props.html: He’s a folk and Americana songwriter based just outside Denver, with six records behind him, King of the Mountain and Here and Now Is Home among them, and an NPR Tiny Desk Contest entry every year since 2019. He calls it heady folk for the open-hearted. He joined the roster under his own name in September 2026.

Solo, he’s played the listening venues around Denver, Swallow Hill and the Black Rose Acoustic Society among them, and stages at the Denver Botanic Gardens and the Clyfford Still Museum. With the four piece, the same songs get lead guitar, bass and drums under them, which is the band you can watch on a Denver club stage and at the Underground Music Showcase in the footage below, and the band that played the Boulder Roots Music Fest.

rows.term: Wedding ceremonies and the hour after
rows.text: Solo voice and acoustic guitar plays the ceremony, then the cocktail hour at a volume the receiving line talks across. It sounds like one person singing to the people in front of him, and the hour can be his own songs, covers, or both.
The evening after a day of sessions, on a deck or around a fire, solo or with the trio, at a level people can talk over and worth listening to when they stop.
A dinner for twenty or a house concert for fifty, where his own songs get the whole crowd’s attention. Solo is the size indoors, and the trio fits a backyard.

He’s a featured artist of the Denver Public Library’s Volume Denver program, so a library afternoon or a market morning is a natural solo booking, and the band plays the park stage a city’s summer series books. Send us the call for performers and we answer it with the size that fits the stage.

props.html: How the music sits around speeches and a program is planned with the run of show. What live music costs across Colorado, size by size, is set out in the cost guide.

items.a: His own songs. He's a folk and Americana songwriter on voice and acoustic guitar with six records behind him, booked through Signet Artists in Denver, and the footage on this page is him playing his own songs solo and with his band. Covers go into the set when you ask for them.

items.q: Does he play covers at a private event?
items.a: Yes, beside his own songs. The covers on this page run from Willie Nelson and The Beatles to The Cars, and a set can lean toward the songs your guests already know or toward his own, so tell us the night and the balance you want.

Solo, it's a voice and a guitar at the level of the conversation, so a receiving line or a dinner table talks across it, and a listening crowd hears every word. The four piece with drums plays a park stage or a summer party like a band. He sets the level to the space and the crowd.

Yes. Solo plays a patio, a garden or a farmers market on one circuit of power with the sound support included, and the band plays a park stage or a lawn with a sound system behind it. Tell us the venue and we'll bring the size that suits it.
